SUSD Controller, Other RTOS Apps), whereas Image 2 includes many more lifelines: VIP CDD and Autosar, System State Controller, SoC PLC State Controller, SoC HW, BSP/RTOS, libclmclien, vcu_ham_lib, RTOS App... SUSD Controller, RTOS Others, Android VHAL / PowerModing Service, Android OS/FW, and Android CPMS. 3) Flow and Interactions: Image 1 shows a simplified flow with events like SUSD_PLC_STATE_RTOS_SHUTDOWN_PULLBACK(), finished(), wait(), some power level reports, heartbeat control, and the resetting of VCUs. Image 2 contains a detailed flow of RTOS suspend preparation, loops and timers for shutdown phases, synchronization requests, logging, power level reporting, driver suspend/shutdown, and Android suspend completion signaling. Multiple alt and loop constructs are present in Image 2 with extensive notes and conditions not seen in Image 1. 4) Actions and Conditions: Image 2 includes significant new content about timers (PLC_RTOS_SHUTDOWN_P1_TIMER, PLC_SoC_SHUTDOWNP1_TIMER, PLC_SoC_SHUTDOWNP2_TIMER), Android suspend/shutdown interaction, file system sync, loggings such as 1) Log application names... 2) Take call logs..., as well as detailed notes explaining steps and failure recovery, which are not present in Image 1. 5) Additional notes and annotations: Each diagram has unique annotations related to its context—in Image 1, notes about VIP restart and SOH messages continuation post-pullback, and in Image 2, notes about stopping HAM process monitoring, pending writes flush, notifying suspend fault, system state controller notification, initiating low level shutdown recovery, and ignoring shutdown requests in some cases. These combined differences show Image 2 is an extended, much more detailed process diagram compared to the simpler pullback focus diagram in Image 1.

DEFINITIONS

NON-INFORMATIONAL IMAGE — a blank/rectangle/block with no content, a single horizontal/ vertical line or divider, a watermark or logo or brand mark or graphic (no meaningful surrounding text/ data/ information), a standalone section number (e.g. 5.2.1)

INFORMATIONAL IMAGE means - Meaningful sentences, paragraphs, labels, tables with data or text in cells, Diagrams, flowcharts, charts, or illustrations with labels, any image combining a logo/watermark WITH other meaningful content (e.g., a watermarked page with text), any image that contains readable text or diagram or data or charts or flow etc that conveys MEANINGFUL information, even if it also contains a logo/watermark.

TRIVIAL DIFFERENCES include: layout shifts, resizing, resolution or quality differences, punctuation-only differences, spelling mistakes, watermark additions/removals, minor color shade, compression differences with no content impact.

MEANINGFUL CHANGES include: Any change that alters the information conveyed e.g. Words added, removed, or replaced, Numbers, dates, or values changed that conveys meaningful impact • Sentences reworded or restructured with meaningful impact • Rows/columns added or removed in a table • Cell content changed in a table • Diagram elements added, removed, or reconnected or text in diagrams being changed • Flow changed in a flowchart ETC. — any change that alters the information conveyed by the image • Labels, captions, or headings or text changed meaningfully in a way that alters the information conveyed • One of the many diagrams in an image being crossed out partially is also a meaningful change.

           → discard_image = true
